concepts.why: The presence of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components, as well as the involvement of the left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots, supports the diagnosis of a maxillary sinus tumor.
The symptoms of sinus pressure and facial swelling, along with the presence of a left nasal mass and mild left-sided proptosis, are consistent with juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma.

The presence of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components, as well as the involvement of the left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots, could also suggest a maxillary sinus cyst.

The symptoms of mild left-sided proptosis and the presence of a heterogeneous mass eroding the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells, could be consistent with an orbital inflammatory pseudotumor.

The presence of a spindle cell process in a patternless arrangement with significant multinucleated giant cells, rare mitotic activity, and no cytologic atypia, supports the diagnosis of a giant cell tumor.

aliases: Fibrous dysplasia of the maxillofacial region
